questions.question: What input and output shapes fit MNISTModel for a batch of 64 flattened images?
questions.explanation: The first Linear expects 784 features per image, and the final Linear emits ten class logits for each of the 64 rows.

questions.question: What should be passed to nn.CrossEntropyLoss in this MNIST loop?
options: Softmax probabilities with one-hot floating labels only
Raw logits with shape [batch,10] and integer class labels
Thresholded class indices as both inputs and targets
The model's hidden ReLU activations and image pixels
questions.explanation: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss combines log-softmax with the negative log likelihood and expects class-index targets, so the model should return raw logits.

questions.question: Which order matches train_one_epoch in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Gradients are cleared before the forward pass, computed from loss.backward(), and applied by optimizer.step().

questions.question: Why does evaluate call model.eval() and use torch.no_grad()?
options: It makes the test labels trainable parameters
It forces every model output to be zero
Evaluation disables training-time layers such as Dropout and avoids building gradient graphs
questions.explanation: eval() changes module behavior, while no_grad() saves memory and computation because no parameter update follows.

questions.question: In demo_autograd, y=x^2+3x and x=[1,2,3]. What gradient does z=sum(y) produce?
questions.explanation: dy/dx=2x+3, giving [5,7,9]. Summing y supplies an upstream gradient of one to each element.

questions.question: What shape does x.unsqueeze(0) have when x was created with torch.randn(3,4)?
questions.explanation: unsqueeze(0) inserts a new leading dimension of size one, turning [3,4] into [1,3,4].
